classical_comparator.note: a LINEAR classical model on the SAME positional features scores 1.0000 on the same held-out words. The circuit matches it; it does not beat it.

meta_notes.headline: S-real 1.0000 +/- 0.0000 (5/5 seeds), S-scramble 0.6567 +/- 0.1558, floor 0.5033 +/- 0.0332. The circuit binds a REAL morphological contrast and transfers it to words never seen in training, and the binding is POSITIONAL -- destroying character order costs 0.343.
meta_notes.resolution: doc 51 SS11.5 pre-registered that the scramble arm might be unresolvable at n=8. It IS resolved: the gap is 0.3433 against a standard error of 0.0697 on the S-scramble mean, ~4.9 SE. The caveat does not bite.
meta_notes.NOT_quantum: doc 47 SS14 applies and here it is MEASURED, not argued: a linear classical model on the identical positional features reaches 1.0000 on the same held-out words. The contribution is the ENCODING DESIGN, not the quantum component. No quantum-advantage reading is licensed and none is registered.
meta_notes.scope: One contrast, one inventory (24 nouns, 8 held out), simulation. WORD-holdout not root-holdout (SS11.8: one word per root). S-scramble's high variance (0.467-0.822) reflects residual non-positional signal the scrambled map retains (test bound 0.9333).
